races.nomineesSource: Alaska's top-four nonpartisan primary on Aug. 18, 2026 advanced Mary Peltola (D), Sen. Dan Sullivan (R), Gerald Heikes (R) and Dan J. Sullivan (No Party Affiliation) to the ranked-choice general election; Peltola led Sen. Sullivan by about 8 points in the final unofficial primary tally. Sources: KTOO/Alaska Public Media, 'U.S. Senate race will have two Dan Sullivans and a Mary Peltola' (https://www.ktoo.org/2026/08/18/u-s-senate-race-will-have-two-dan-sullivans-and-a-mary-peltola/); Juneau Independent (https://www.juneauindependent.com/post/peltola-leads-sullivan-by-8-in-final-unofficial-primary-tally-focus-now-on-dropouts-in-governor-s).

result.call: Called by AP on Nov. 17, 2026 (some outlets dated reports Nov. 18), after election officials confirmed Peltola held more than 50% of first-choice votes; no ranked-choice tabulation was needed.
result.figuresAsOf: First-choice (round one) unofficial results with about 99% counted, as reported in AP coverage at the Nov. 17, 2026 call; one report put Peltola at 50.12%. Percentages and vote counts may come from slightly different snapshots.

statements.text: Sullivan joined Sen. John Cornyn and 11 other senators in introducing the FIGHT China Act, which would have Treasury prohibit or require notice of certain U.S. investments in Chinese technologies, including artificial intelligence and advanced semiconductors.
statements.headline: Co-led bill restricting U.S. investment in Chinese AI

source.title: Sen. Dan Sullivan: Sullivan, Cornyn, and Colleagues Introduce Outbound Investment Legislation to Counter China (Mar. 14, 2025)

statements.notes: Cornyn's office dates the introduction Mar. 13, 2025; Sullivan's release is dated Mar. 14. Cornyn's office reports the outbound investment provisions passed the Senate on Dec. 17, 2025 and were signed into law Dec. 19, 2025 via the defense bill (https://www.cornyn.senate.gov/news/cornyn-cortez-masto-colleagues-outbound-investment-measures-signed-into-law); not checked against congressional records. statements.text: The Senate voted 99-1 to adopt Sen. Marsha Blackburn's amendment removing a 10-year moratorium on state AI regulation from the reconciliation bill; Sen. Thom Tillis cast the only no vote, so Sullivan voted to remove the moratorium.
statements.headline: Voted to strip state AI-law moratorium from budget bill

statements.notes: Sullivan's individual vote is inferred from the 99-1 tally with Tillis as the sole no; the sources found do not name Sullivan.

statements.text: In his annual address to the Alaska Legislature, Sullivan listed Air Force data centers on Alaska bases, which would increase demand for natural gas, among recent progress, according to a Must Read Alaska summary. Newsweek separately reported that Sullivan petitioned to bring data centers onto Air Force and joint military installations and, with Gov. Mike Dunleavy, presented Alaska's cold climate and North Slope gas reserves as advantages for attracting AI data centers.
statements.headline: Promoted AI data centers on Alaska military bases

source.title: Must Read Alaska: Sullivan Touts 'Alaska Comeback,' Historic Opportunities, in Annual Address to Legislature (Feb. 2026)

statements.notes: The data center reference in the speech comes from a secondhand summary; the official transcript (https://www.sullivan.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sullivan-touts-alaska-comeback-historic-opportunities-in-annual-address-to-legislature) was not viewed. Neither Newsweek piece gives a date or direct quote for Sullivan's data center advocacy. The Air Force issued its request for lease proposals for AI data centers at JBER, Eielson AFB and Clear SFS on Apr. 10, 2026.

statements.text: Sullivan's office said he authored provisions in the Senate Armed Services Committee's FY2027 defense authorization bill, including one directing the Department of War to set up a strategy and roadmap to reduce local community impacts while private data centers are built on military installations. The committee approved the bill 18-9.
statements.headline: NDAA provision on data center impacts near bases

gaps: KS: No statements by Adam Hamilton on AI beyond data centers (AI safety, children, deepfakes, preemption, jobs, chips) were found.
KS: A Sept. 12, 2026 debate claim by Hamilton that a bill Marshall voted for gave $30 billion in tax cuts to data centers appears only in a partisan blog fact-check (wichitaliberty.org); left out.

KS: Marshall co-introduced the Aging with Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026 with Sens. Mark Kelly and Rick Scott (Senate Aging Committee release), and chaired a HELP subcommittee hearing on AI in health care; dates not confirmed, so not entered as statements.

KS/ME: Marshall's and Collins's individual votes on the Sept. 30, 2026 Ratepayer Protection Act cloture motion are inferred from the 57-43 tally and Newsweek's list (Collins's yes vote is also reported by Newsweek). Not checked against the Senate roll call.
KS: Kansas State Board of Canvassers certification not yet found (2024 precedent: Dec. 3). Libertarian David Graham's vote total not retrieved.

KS: No Kansas-only poll figures on AI or data centers found. The 2026 Kansas Speaks survey (FHSU Docking Institute) asked about data centers, but its percentages were not retrieved. Newsweek reports fewer than 1% of Kansas respondents in a NYT/Siena poll named data centers their top issue; dates and sample not found.

KS: An Emerson poll from Sept. 15-16, 2026 reportedly ranked economy 48%, health care 14%, threats to democracy 9%, housing affordability 9%, education 6%. Left out because its source URL could not be pinned down.
ME: The NPR quote of Jackson calling for 'real guardrails' on data centers was not found in this round; the closest verbatim debate quote is 'real parameters, real guidelines' (Newsweek).
ME: Only early first-choice AP figures (4:38 a.m. Nov. 4) were found; no final count, ranked-choice tabulation or Secretary of State certification found.

ME: Collins's cosponsorship of the Senate Ratepayer Protection Act is reported only by The American Prospect. No 2026 Collins statements found on children and AI, federal preemption of state AI laws, or AI and jobs.
ME: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act item is dated from the Sept. 2023 Klobuchar release; whether the Collins release describes a later reintroduction is not confirmed.

ME: For the NYT/Siena September Maine poll (66% oppose data centers; 41% Jackson vs. 39% Collins on data centers; MoE 5.4 per Newsweek), the field dates, sample size and release date were not found. Newsweek did not name the pollster; the attribution comes from a search summary citing the Boston Globe.

ME: Fox News Maine Aug. 6-10 poll: only inflation (32%, from a Fox video description) and immigration (18%, Newsweek) were retrieved; health care and political divisions percentages not found. AARP Maine poll (Sept. 20-22, 982 likely voters) ranked affordability, threats to democracy and immigration as top issues but percentages not retrieved. UNH Pine Tree State Poll (Feb. 2026) lists cost of living and housing as top problems without retrieved percentages.
OH: No Sherrod Brown statements on AI beyond data centers were found.

OH: The AP call time (11:11 p.m. ET) comes from a single report. Redpath and Levy vote totals not retrieved. No Ohio certification announcement found (county official canvass was due within 21 days, by Nov. 24).

OH: Fox News Ohio May 28-June 1 poll: only the inflation share (43%) of the top-issue question was retrieved. A Fox Aug. 6-10 Ohio poll had inflation at 40%. Marist and AARP Ohio polls cited personal finances and affordability without retrieved percentages.

OH: The Ohio Northern University Northern Poll reportedly found 55% of Ohio adults oppose data center construction in their communities and 57% support legal restrictions or megawatt caps; date and URL not found. The BGSU September poll's publication date and the NYT/Siena Ohio poll's field dates were not found.

OH: Husted's Senate Ratepayer Protection Act bill number (S. 5028 in one summary) was not verified. Husted's 'hypocrite' reply to Brown's ads (Signal Cleveland) is undated. The air dates of Brown's data center ads are inconsistent across outlets.

Iowa: final unofficial vote totals and percentages (including Libertarian Thomas Laehn's share) not found; only the Nov. 3 partial count (Turek 50.8%, Hinson 46.1%) was available. The exact time of the AP call was not found.

Iowa: no 2026 certification date or announcement from the State Board of Canvassers found. A Nov. 13, 2026 report said Secretary of State Paul Pate defended the midterm results (https://www.wowt.com/2026/11/13/iowa-secretary-state-defends-midterm-election-results/); the nature of the challenge was not researched.

Hinson: no statement on data centers (local moratoriums, electricity rates, water, tax breaks) found. Her individual votes on the House-passed One Big Beautiful Bill Act's 10-year state AI-law moratorium (May 2025) and on the Ratepayer Protection Act (passed 417-3 on Sept. 16, 2026) were not confirmed by name; a CAP Action report says almost every House Republican voted for the moratorium version but the excerpt seen did not name Hinson. No AI bill sponsored by Hinson was found.

Turek: no direct statement on AI (safety, children, deepfakes, preemption, jobs, chips) found, and no detailed data center position; the only item is a Semafor search snippet. Newsweek characterized his campaign as focused on opposing 'billionaires and large corporations' rather than a detailed data center platform.

Peltola: no AI-general statements found, and no AI-related votes or bills from her House tenure (2022-2025) found. Newsweek said her campaign focused on affordability and energy costs generally rather than data centers specifically. The date and venue of her 'pay their own way' remarks were not identified.

Sullivan: no direct quote on data centers found; his data center advocacy is reported secondhand (Must Read Alaska, Newsweek). His 99-1 vote to strip the state AI moratorium is inferred from the tally. No statement on AI and children, deepfakes or jobs found.

Alaska: certification by the Nov. 25, 2026 target not confirmed. The Justice Department sued on Oct. 22 to block certification if Sullivan lost; Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed the suit Nov. 1, and an appeal and a federal criminal investigation tied to the second Dan Sullivan's candidacy were reported pending. Sullivan's campaign said he would not concede before certification.

Alaska polls: AARP's other issue percentages (threats to democracy; taxes, spending and debt) not found. An Alaska Current item described a poll (Oct. 17-23, year unclear) in which economy, jobs and inflation ranked highest, without percentages. No Alaska poll asking about AI or data centers was found.

Iowa polls: publication dates for the Emerson October and September releases were not confirmed (recorded as month only). The Fox News poll's population is listed as registered voters per one summary; the horse-race figures were reported among likely voters, and the margin of error was not found. A July 2026 Fox News Iowa poll found 39% named inflation as most important, but its field dates were not found, so it is omitted.
